questions.prompt: What is Next.js's default rendering strategy for a route with no request-specific data?

options.text: Static rendering at build time, reused for every request
It never renders until a user interacts

questions.explanation: By default Next.js statically renders routes at build time and reuses that HTML for all requests.

questions.prompt: Which of these are Dynamic APIs that switch a route to dynamic rendering? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: cookies(), headers(), draftMode(), and searchParams are Dynamic APIs. Importing CSS has nothing to do with rendering strategy.

questions.prompt: To force a route to always render at request time, export: export const dynamic = '______'.
questions.explanation: export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' pins a route to dynamic rendering; 'force-static' pins it static.

questions.prompt: Match each term or page to its rendering strategy.
questions.explanation: SSG is static, SSR is dynamic; shared content suits static rendering while per-user pages suit dynamic.

questions.prompt: Order the decision Next.js makes for a route (default 'auto').

items.text: Does the route use a Dynamic API (cookies, headers, searchParams)?
If no, render it statically at build time
If yes, render it dynamically per request

questions.explanation: With dynamic = 'auto', Next.js checks for Dynamic APIs; without them the route is static, with them it's dynamic.
